events.continuity_hook: Continues the Chicago training episode after the official hotel block sold out and the closer backup hotel became the likely replacement.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the hotel booking, pair it cleanly with the approved flight plan, and leave only breakfast, arrival meal, and seat details for the final check.
events.scenario_brief: The Chicago training booking is almost complete. The closer backup hotel a few blocks from the Loop meeting center is approved as long as Maya books the refundable rate and notes that breakfast is not included. The suite property is still cheaper but would add a less predictable morning commute. Her flights remain the Monday afternoon nonstop into O'Hare and a Thursday afternoon return. She needs to lock the hotel, add a quiet-room request, verify practical breakfast options nearby, and check whether a window seat has opened on either leg.

events.continuity_hook: Wraps the Chicago training planning with the flight timing stable and the replacement hotel confirmed.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the keep-as-booked Chicago plan and produce a concise travel-day and first-morning checklist.
events.scenario_brief: A couple of days before the Chicago departure, the organizer confirms that Thursday's closing session should end by noon, so Maya can keep the afternoon return. The closer backup hotel is booked near the meeting center, but breakfast is still a paid option and Monday evening arrival may be close to dinner time. She wants one final pass covering Atlanta airport timing, O'Hare-to-Loop transfer, hotel check-in, Tuesday's 8:30 a.m. start, nearby dinner choices, breakfast workarounds, weather, and any newly available window seats.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new work-travel episode after the Chicago training trip is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Denver trip, identify workable Atlanta flight windows and likely hotel areas, and list the client details needed before routing the plan for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from Chicago, Maya is assigned to a Denver-area client configuration workshop for Monday, December 8 through Thursday, December 11. The draft agenda has full client days on Tuesday and Wednesday plus a likely Thursday debrief, but the exact office address is not confirmed and no one has said whether Monday evening setup is needed. From Atlanta, she wants straightforward winter travel, no messy routing, and a hotel that will not make early client mornings difficult. The unresolved pieces are whether the client site is downtown or in the Tech Center area, how late Thursday will run, and whether a rental car is worth considering.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Denver planning after the client confirms the Tech Center location and reduces the Monday arrival pressure.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the strongest flight-and-hotel combinations, weigh commute certainty against included breakfast, and choose the package to send for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms the workshop will be in Greenwood Village near the Denver Tech Center, with Tuesday starting at 9:00 a.m. and Monday evening setup now optional. Maya is comparing a Monday afternoon Delta nonstop that gets her to the hotel before dinner with a cheaper one-stop itinerary that lands close to bedtime. For Thursday, a mid-afternoon nonstop looks efficient if the debrief ends by lunch, while an early evening nonstop gives more cushion. The hotel choice is between a highly rated business hotel close to the client office with on-site dining but paid breakfast, and a suite-style property with included breakfast but a longer rideshare each morning. She is still deciding whether to avoid a rental car.

events.continuity_hook: Keeps the Denver work trip moving after approval, with the outbound flight and hotel stable but the return timing newly uncertain.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the mid-afternoon and later nonstop returns, decide which one fits the updated agenda, and prepare a brief explanation for the fare difference if needed.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Monday afternoon nonstop and the closer Denver Tech Center hotel, with the expectation that she will use rideshare instead of renting a car. Then the client moves the Thursday debrief later, now expected to run until about 1:30 or 2:00 p.m. The mid-afternoon return from Denver becomes tight because of the airport distance, while a later nonstop is still available at a moderate fare increase. One-stop returns do not save enough to make the extra moving parts worthwhile. She needs to decide whether to switch the return before the fare changes.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-trip check for the Denver client workshop after the return flight was moved later to protect the Thursday schedule.
events.interaction_goal: Create a concise Denver travel checklist and flag the last items to verify before leaving for the airport.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before the Denver departure, Maya has the Monday afternoon nonstop, the later Thursday nonstop, and the closer Tech Center hotel booked. Light snow is possible on arrival evening, and the hotel does not include breakfast, but it has an on-site restaurant and several nearby options. She wants a final rundown covering Atlanta airport timing, Denver arrival and rideshare logistics, hotel check-in, dinner after arrival, breakfast options before the Tuesday client start, the morning commute to the client office, receipt handling for rideshares, and whether any better window seat choices have opened.
